newsitem.title: FRANCE: Maystadt sees bilateral contribs to IMF's ESAF.
newsitem.headline: Maystadt sees bilateral contribs to IMF's ESAF.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Thursday he believed bilateral contributions could make up the majority of the funding requirement for IMF funds for poorer nations.

Maystadt, who is chairman of the International Monetary Fund's interim committee, was asked at a news conference whether there would be agreement on selling IMF gold to fund the IMF's enhanced structural adjustment facility (ESAF).
"There may be a consensus on other means...certainly not for the whole amount," he said. "There may be bilateral contributions for the majority of the amounts needed."
He said the IMF would first seek to establish how much countries were willing to put in in bilateral contributions but said he expected them to make "a special effort".
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told the same news conference that France wanted an agreement on funding ESAF reached by consensus.
Germany and some other countries oppose selling a small part of the IMF's gold reserves to provide financing for the ESAF.
Some officials in rich countries have suggested the question of whether or not gold should be sold should be put to a vote at the IMF.
